content.title: About
content.content: Decaffeinated coffee pre‑sweetened with sugar is a ground or instant coffee from which the natural caffeine has been removed and sugar has been added for a mild sweetness. The drink retains the aromatic notes of regular coffee but lacks the stimulating effect.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Decaffeination is usually performed by water extraction or super‑critical CO₂, preserving most flavor compounds.
Adding sugar makes the beverage popular with children and those who prefer a sweet taste without milk or cream.
Decaf coffee may still contain up to 0.1 % of the original caffeine, which is considered safe for caffeine‑sensitive individuals.
Sugar accelerates caramelization during roasting, giving a deeper aroma.
In some countries decaffeinated coffee is classified as a separate product and requires distinct labeling.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Even without caffeine, decaf coffee retains polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Coffee stimulates gastric juice production, which can aid digestion without the risk of caffeine‑induced irritation.

items.title: Source of magnesium
items.content: Magnesium in coffee supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: May lower risk of certain diseases
items.content: Regular moderate consumption of decaf coffee is linked to a reduced risk of type 2 diabetes and some cancers.

items.title: Quick energy source
items.content: Added sugar provides an immediate glucose boost, useful when fast energy is needed.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The added sugar makes the drink caloric; people with diabetes or weight‑control goals should monitor portion size.

items.title: Coffee allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to coffee components.

items.title: Residual caffeine
items.content: Some decaffeination methods leave trace amounts of caffeine, which could affect highly sensitive persons.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Coffee remains acidic and may irritate the stomach of those with gastritis or ulcers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Place 1‑2 tsp of ground coffee into 200 ml of hot (not boiling) water, stir, and let steep for 3‑5 minutes. Milk, cream, or spices can be added to taste. The pre‑sweetened version usually does not require extra sugar.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the coffee in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. Keep moisture away to prevent clumping and flavor loss. Shelf life is typically 12 months.
